item.title: Andy Reid provides update on wife of Eric Bieniemy, who was allegedly shot by own son
item.description: Andy Reid says Mia Bieniemy is out of the ICU after suffering multiple gunshot wounds at the family's Ashburn, Virginia, home earlier this week.
item.content:encoded:
Andy Reid gave a positive update on the wife of Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy, who was shot earlier this week.

Mia Bieniemy suffered "multiple gunshot wounds" at the couple's home in Ashburn, Virginia, and was originally in stable condition and hospitalized.

"She's doing great. She's doing better and great from where she was," Reid told reporters from training camp on Wednesday. "Out of the ICU unit, happy about that. EB is still with her, that part's important."

Loudoun County Sheriff's Office spokesperson Leah Pau said Monday that police arrived at a home located on the 20000 block of Northpark Drive in Ashburn, Virginia, Sunday evening and arrested the couple's 27-year-old son, Elijah Zion Bieniemy. He was arrested on charges of malicious wounding, use of a firearm in commission of a felony, and discharge of a firearm inside a dwelling, according to a press release by the Loudon County Sheriff's Office.

NFL STAR SAQUON BARKLEY IS ALL FOR MLB PLAYERS FIGHTING AGAINST SALARY CAP: 'IT SHOULD HAPPEN'

Elijah was also transported to the Loudon County Adult Detention Center where he is being held without bond.

The Chiefs had coaches, rookies and quarterbacks report to camp at St. Joseph, Missouri, on the campus of Missouri Western State, on Friday. Veteran players reported on Tuesday.

Bieniemy, 56, returned to the Chiefs this year as their offensive coordinator after spending time with the Washington Commanders, Chicago Bears and UCLA's football program.

As offensive coordinator in Kansas City from 2018-22, Bieniemy oversaw one of the league's most productive offenses to become an AFC stalwart, winning two Super Bowls in his tenure.

OutKick's Armando Salguero contributed to this report.

item.title: Jared Leto responds to sexual misconduct allegations made by multiple women in explosive documentary
item.description: Jared Leto denies sexual assault allegations from four women who claim offenses occurred when they were teenagers, calling the claims "categorically false."
item.content:encoded:
Jared Leto is denying allegations of criminal sexual conduct after four women accused the Oscar-winning actor and musician of offenses they claim occurred when they were teenagers.

"I have never sexually assaulted anyone in my entire life," Leto said in a statement provided to Fox News Digital. "These claims are absolutely and categorically false."

The allegations are detailed in the new BBC documentary "Jared Leto: Hollywood's Dark Secret," which premiered Wednesday. The film features interviews with 10 participants, nine of whom shared their stories publicly for the first time.

According to the documentary, four women allege Leto engaged in criminal sexual conduct between 2002 and 2016, when the actor and Thirty Seconds to Mars frontman — now 54 — was in his 30s and 40s.

JASON ALEXANDER APOLOGIZES AFTER COURTNEY STODDEN SAYS 2012 COMEDY SKETCH OBJECTIFIED HER AS A MINOR

In a BBC story published on Wednesday, one woman alleged she had sex with Leto at his California home when she was 17 years old. According to the outlet, the woman said Leto, who was 34 at the time, dismissed concerns after they discussed California's age of consent being 18.

"It wasn't a huge concern for him," she alleged. "He told me, 'I would like you to call me daddy.' And it was either pretend to be a little girl or 'my little girl.'"

The woman said that because she was "so naive and vulnerable" at the time, she didn't understand that this behavior wasn't "normal" in an adult relationship.

"It was only as time went on that I realized more and more how scary that really was," she said.

OSCAR WINNER JARED LETO ADMITS DEPTHS OF DRUG ADDICTION: 'IT TOOK ME FOR A RIDE'

A second woman alleged Leto sexually assaulted her in what she described as a "dingy gross motel" in Las Vegas in 2002, saying he invited her there after meeting her at the store where she worked.

According to the documentary, the woman said Leto called her into the bathroom while he was showering.

"I don't think there was many words exchanged and he opened the shower curtain and started kissing me," she alleged.

She claimed Leto then grabbed her hand and forced her to masturbate him.

"Most of my life I had viewed this event as, I was a stupid girl… and so this bad thing happened," she said.

A third woman alleged Leto threatened her with sexual assault after inviting her to a hotel room in London following a Thirty Seconds to Mars concert in 2013.

The former model said she was 19 at the time, but told Leto she was 17 because she "felt the need" to pretend to be younger to protect herself. After telling Leto she was 17, the woman claimed he said, "Age is just a number, and anyway, we're in Europe."

JARED LETO RECALLS ‘NEARLY DYING’ WHILE ROCK CLIMBING

The woman claimed one of Leto's assistants encouraged her to join in on another party at a nearby hotel room. However, when she arrived, she realized there was no party.

"I get into the hotel room, it's really dark, and then I see that it's just him," she said. "Weren't there supposed to be other people?"

The woman claimed she asked Leto for a phone charger or some cash to get home, but he dismissed her requests.

After asking if she could sleep on a chaise lounge because she had no way home, the woman claimed Leto repeatedly told her she would wake up "with a d— in her ass."

After realizing she "was not safe," the woman left the room.

A fourth woman said Leto began grooming her when she was 16, made repeated sexually explicit phone calls to her and on at least one occasion suggested the two have sex.

According to the BBC, the woman was later presented with a nondisclosure agreement intended to prevent her from discussing her alleged relationship with Leto. She declined to sign the document, which BBC said they had reviewed.

Additional women also accused the actor of making what they described as "strange" and sexually explicit phone calls while they were underage or teenagers.

The documentary also featured interviews with two former employees connected to Thirty Seconds to Mars, who claim staff members were uncomfortable with Leto's interactions with teenage girls.

One former employee alleged Leto would invite teenage girls backstage to his dressing room or to a house where the band was recording.

"I think everyone thought the age gap was way too big," the former employee said.

The allegations are the latest in a series of claims against the Academy Award winner.

In June 2025, Air Mail published interviews with nine women who alleged Leto engaged in inappropriate sexual behavior over the years, including accusations involving minors. Those allegations included claims that Leto asked sexually explicit questions to a 16-year-old, exposed himself to a 17-year-old and placed an 18-year-old's hand "on him."

The Air Mail report followed allegations by Los Angeles DJ Allie Teilz, who publicly claimed she was assaulted by Leto when she was 17.

At the time, representatives for Leto "expressly" denied the Air Mail allegations, calling Teilz's claims "demonstrably false."

According to the BBC, Leto did not respond to repeated requests for comment regarding the documentary's allegations.

item.title: Coffee slushie is summer's hottest drink but expert warns one mistake can turn it 'into more of a dessert'
item.description: The viral coffee slushie trend works with cold brew or hot coffee, but a dietitian warns flavored syrups can quietly turn it into a dessert.
item.content:encoded:
Coffee lovers have found their latest summer obsession: the coffee slushie.

The icy drink has been making the rounds on social media, with home baristas freezing brewed coffee before blending it into a frosty, caffeine-packed treat.

While the frozen beverage looks indulgent, experts say the drink itself isn't necessarily any less healthy than your usual cup of joe. Rather, it all depends on what you add to it.

SCIENTISTS USED ELECTRICITY ON COFFEE AND DISCOVERED WHAT MAKES IT TASTE GOOD

"Honestly, the frozen format itself doesn't make coffee any more or less healthy than drinking it hot," South Carolina-based dietitian nutritionist Lauren Manaker told Fox News Digital. "It's still just coffee, just colder and more fun for summer."

In fact, a homemade coffee slushie can be a smarter choice than other frozen beverages, Manaker said.

"A homemade coffee slushie can actually be a healthier option, since traditional slushies are typically loaded with added sugars and offer little nutritional value," she said.

To make the drink more satisfying, she recommends using dairy milk.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"Opting for dairy milk brings a unique combination of 13 essential nutrients and quality protein together that can help you feel more satiated, all with no added sugars," Manaker said. "If you're lactose intolerant, lactose-free dairy milk is a great option that keeps those same nutritional benefits intact, just without the lactose."

The biggest nutritional pitfall isn't the coffee but the extras, Manaker cautioned.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"Flavored syrups, sweetened creamers and sugary toppings are what can quietly turn your everyday iced coffee into more of a dessert," she said.

Chandra Holt, the Texas-based founder of Incredibrew, said coffee naturally lends itself to the frozen format.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"A cup of coffee is 95% water, so if you freeze it, you don't need to add ice, so it makes a great slushie," she said, adding that the recipe works with either cold brew or hot coffee that's been cooled before freezing.

For the best flavor, Holt recommends brewing a stronger batch.

"The key is using strong coffee so you get a lot of coffee flavor after you add the milk," she noted.

item.title: NCAA suspends Tennessee linebacker for $427 plane ticket, as college sports hands out millions in NIL
item.description: Tennessee's Arion Carter returned from injury to play college football, but the NCAA suspended him two games for accepting a flight from an NFL agent.
item.content:encoded:
The NCAA has lost another battle in the court of public opinion, and this time it involves a college football player at Tennessee.

In a world in which college athletes are being paid millions of dollars to play, it looks as though the NCAA is still harping on the small things like we are still living in the past. Should this come as a surprise? Probably not, given the organization is still trying to hold onto any power they have left within this current ecosystem of college athletics.

Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter has been suspended two games by the NCAA for accepting a flight paid for by an NFL agent after he decided that he would try his hand at professional football after the 2025 season and signed with representation.

Tick Tock: SEC and Big Ten receive revised Protect College Sports Act as Senate vote timeline looms

How much was the plane ticket? A measly $427 that only came when Carter decided to enter the 2026 NFL Draft. This violation, which is a Level III, is pretty far down the totem pole when it comes to NCAA standards on rules.

But, because Carter had accepted this travel from a professional agent, compared to the hundreds of NIL or college agents that are roaming throughout college athletics, it doesn’t matter that Arion had repaid the $427 earlier this year.

Yes, you read that right. In a world in which much more egregious rules will be broken on a random Tuesday, Carter is being punished for signing with an NFL agent and accepting an airline ticket.

Don't get me wrong, I understand the NCAA has a rule that says if a player declares for the draft and signs with an agent, he cannot return to the collegiate ranks.

But, these were uncharted waters, given Arion Carter was hurt very early in the process, and did the smart thing by returning to college.

It wasn’t as if he waited until three weeks before the NFL Draft. In reality, there needs to be a process for players to return if something like this happens. Carter wasn’t chasing a lucrative bag, given that he had already declared and Tennessee even announced his intentions.

COLLEGE SPORTS SEES PIVOTAL MOMENT AS SENATE LOOKS TO MOVE LEGISLATION ON NIL, TRANSFERS ACROSS GOAL LINE

We have athletes that have played professional baseball for ten years currently on rosters in college football.

But, the NCAA draws the line and also states he should actually be indefinitely suspended, so they are doing Carter a favor by only handing down a 2-game judgement (after they initially wanted 3 games).

After declaring for the NFL Draft, the Tennessee linebacker started the process of working out in preparation for his professional career. It was during one of those workouts where Arion Carter suffered an injury that forced him to make a decision about whether he should return for one more season of college football.

Ultimately, he decided to take his name out of the NFL Draft process and return to Tennessee for the upcoming season.

At last week's SEC Media Days in Tampa, Carter represented the Vols and had this to say about returning to Tennessee after a setback.

"Coming back off my injury and ultimately choosing to come back to the University of Tennessee was a pivotal point in my life. I fell like I made the greatest decision I possibly could have made," Carter told reporters.

Somewhere in the realm of college athletics at this moment, there is a player cashing a check from a university or third-party collective that is in the five- to six-figure range.

That's the world we live in now, where even high school athletes are being promised private-jet hours to entice them to sign with a school. Heck, there are schools offering athletes actual real estate property for future investments to sign with a college.

Inside the fight: NIL arms race fueling new push for College Football Playoff expansion

Have I mentioned that athletes are making seven-figures a year to play sports at the collegiate level?

"This is ridiculous, if that's exactly how it played out," one Power-4 general manger told OutKick-FOX News. "I just had a player in my office looking for a $30,000 raise before we start Fall camp, and the NCAA is punishing a player for making the right decision when it comes to his long-term viability when trying to play football.

"What are we doing? Look, I usually have zero sympathy for an opposing school we're competing with for players, but I feel horrible for the young man."

Did the NCAA take on Tennessee this aggressively because of past litigation? I mean, possibly, given that the Vols essentially sued the organization in order to steer them away from potential penalties related to the recruitment of Nico Iamaleava years ago.

Sure, there could be pettiness involved here. Or, the NCAA is once again trying to puff their chests out to send a message that they are still in charge of rules and penalties.

Personally, I'm going with the second option.

item.title: Resurfaced video of resident rejecting Fauci’s door-to-door vaccine sales pitch goes viral
item.description: A D.C. resident confronted Anthony Fauci at his door over vaccine safety concerns during the 2021 Anacostia door-to-door campaign with Muriel Bowser.
item.content:encoded:
A resurfaced video of Dr. Anthony Fauci's 2021 door-to-door COVID-19 vaccine campaign is gaining renewed attention amid his contentious testimony before Congress on the federal handling of the pandemic.

The clip shows Fauci, then White House health advisor, and Washington, D.C., Mayor Muriel Bowser visiting residents in the city's Anacostia neighborhood to encourage them to get vaccinations. But the footage shows several skeptical residents challenging Fauci over the vaccines' rapid development, long-term safety and the government's messaging — exchanges that have become a flashpoint in the debate over the federal response.

And now that Fauci's diary has been published and includes seemingly contradictory public statements versus private musings, his entire involvement has come under the microscope of his biggest critics.

"The people in America are not settled with the information that's been given to us right now. So I'm not gonna be lining up taking a shot on a vaccination, for something that wasn't clear in the first place, and then you all create a shot in miraculous time. It takes years to create," said a Washington, D.C. resident in the video shot by PBS in response to Fauci's vaccine push campaign.

DID THE BIDEN ADMINISTRATION PURPOSEFULLY IGNORE COVID VACCINE SIDE EFFECTS?

Fauci and Bowser, who is leaving office at the conclusion of her current term, encouraged residents in the "historic African American neighborhood" of D.C. to get the vaccine, seemingly attempting to persuade skeptical residents and using Fauci as an expert to sway them.

"[If] thousands of people, like you, don't get vaccinated, you're going to let this virus continue to percolate in this country and in this world," urged Bowser, standing alongside the nation's top voice on the coronavirus at the time.

That resident pushed back, continuing to question the very swift timeline of the vaccine's development and roll out. They compared it to the flu and expressed skepticism over why the government was incentivizing residents to get the jab.

FAUCI PRIVATELY TOOK CREDIT FOR COVID-19 LOCKDOWNS DESPITE PUBLIC DENIAL, NEWLY EXPOSED DIARY ENTRIES REVEAL

"Because when you start talking about paying people to get vaccinated, when you start talking about incentivizing things to get people vaccinated, there's something else going on with that. Something else. It's something else," said the resident.

Critics on social media swiftly responded to the resurfaced clip.

"They're terrified of a free-thinking black man. God bless this man," wrote "The Riley Gaines Show" podcast Riley Gaines on X.

"Earlier this day, Fauci learned he had a blood clot in his lung. Yet he still beat on black people’s doors, telling them to get the COVID shots. And these (mad) scientists wonder why black Americans are leery of vaccines? Maybe they don’t want to be Tuskegee test rats again," wrote Article III Project founder Mike Davis.

EXCLUSIVE: BIDEN PARDON WON'T SHIELD FAUCI IF HE LIES TO CONGRESS, COMER SAYS

"Never forget this brave American citizen that turned down getting a Covid vaccine and called out Fauci right to his face on camera," wrote one user on X.

"What an absolute legend this guy… telling that narcissistic, deranged liar and his acolytes to GFT with their sh*tccine," wrote Bitcoin miner Javier Hermonsa.

Fauci and Bowser both did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment on the video making its rounds on social media ahead of the retired medical advisor's appearance in Congress on Wednesday.

Fauci was subpoenaed by Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee Chairman Sen. Rand Paul to answer questions primarily about the U.S. government's handling of COVID-19 and the origins of the virus.

Ahead of the hearing Wednesday morning, President Donald Trump blasted Fauci on Truth Social.

"I Inherited Fauci, who was there since the 1980’s, but with each passing day, relied less and less on him. He made too many bad calls," wrote Trump in part.

"Fauci was largely taken out of play, and then along came Sleepy Joe Biden, who made Fauci a ‘King!’ I called Biden to tell him Fauci was no good, either didn’t have a clue, or was dishonest. The call was well received, but sadly, not acted on. Biden went on to give Fauci vast destructive power," he added.

During the hearing, Fauci repeatedly refused to answer substantive questions, invoking the Fifth Amendment against questions from lawmakers at least 111 times during the hearing.

Paul said the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs will hold a vote next week to "certify" Fauci's contempt of Congress.

item.title: The Nintendo 64 is turning 30 years old, here are some of its most impactful games of all time
item.description: From "Goldeneye 007" to "Ocarina of Time," the N64 turns 30 this summer. These five games defined 3D gaming and still shape the industry today.
item.content:encoded:
If you don't want to feel old, I'd suggest you click away from this article now, but the Nintendo 64 is celebrating its 30th birthday this summer (I warned you).

The console that helped usher 3D gaming into homes everywhere and catapulted us into the fifth generation of gaming has had plenty of legacy-defining games attached to its name.

Today, I want to honor the N64 turning the big 3-0 by looking at some of the most impactful games that were ever released on the console.

Full disclosure, this isn't a "favorites" list.

Some of my favorite and most-played N64 games might not make the list, and there might be a game or two on here that I don't necessarily love.

'HALO' COMPOSER RUNNING FOR CONGRESS DRAWS PARALLELS TO DECLINE OF WOKENESS IN GAMING TO TRUMP'S RE-ELECTION

Conversely, your favorite game might get left off the list, so if that's the case, be sure to scream at me about it in the comments section.

Without further ado, let's talk video games.

We kick this list off with an absolute banger, although, let's be honest, they're all bangers.

"Goldeneye 007" is widely considered one of the most revolutionary first person shooters in gaming history.

The 1997 James Bond movie tie-in took what games like "Doom" and "Wolfenstein" did and brought it into the next generation of gaming.

The gameplay was mind-blowing, especially for the time, but the thing that separated "Goldeneye" from its peers was the multiplayer.

Its four-player "couch multiplayer" set the standard for shooters to come and was so ahead of its time that college dorm rooms still frequent it to this day.

A special mention has to be made to the soundtrack, which has gained an almost cult-like following from both nostalgic Millennials and newer Gen Z fans alike.

If you want an idea of just how impactful a game has become, you'll notice "high-definition remakes" start to pop up years after its release.

"Star Fox 64" is no different, as it has a brand-spanking-new remake out on the Switch 2 nearly three decades after the original.

As far as the N64 version of this game is concerned, there's a reason people have been clamoring for a remake of this game since 1997.

The story of ace pilot Fox McCloud and his misfit crew of anthropomorphic sidekicks has white-knuckle dogfighting, a fun and tightly packed campaign, and more memorable quotes than you could find in any modern movie.

MADDEN 27'S TUSH PUSH TEASE HIGHLIGHTS EVERYTHING WRONG WITH ANNUALLY RELEASED SPORTS GAMES

Seriously, this game spawned the "do a barrel roll" meme that swept the internet in the late 2000s and early 2010s, almost 15 years after the game came out.

If you were looking for a fun crossover between "Star Wars" and "Independence Day" mixed with fun and goofy humor, this was your bag.

Before 1999, the thought of all your favorite video game characters beating the tar out of each other on the same video game console felt like a pipe dream.

That's why "Super Smash Bros." was so Earth-shattering upon its release. It gave every fan something they didn't even know they wanted and set the bar in the process.

Manufacturing a scenario where Link, Samus, Mario, and Fox McCloud could all fight to the death on some of the most iconic Nintendo stages felt like a fever dream.

There were bonus stages, unlockables, and achievements galore, which for the fifth generation of consoles was far ahead of its time.

"Super Smash Bros." created a template for all games to follow after and yet is so unique that it still hasn't been properly imitated or duplicated since.

A true original like this deserves a seat at the table on this list.

The game that started it all, "Super Mario 64" was, surprisingly enough, a launch title for the N64.

Amazingly, one of the best and most impactful games Nintendo has ever created was also the first to be released on their fifth-gen console.

The pairing of Nintendo's most legendary mascot coupled with their first jump into the realm of 3D alone makes this an instant classic, but "Super Mario 64" is more than that.

Every 3D platformer you've ever played owes its very existence to "Super Mario 64," and even 30 years later, the game still holds up.

The soundtrack is iconic, the gameplay is fluid and responsive and rewards skilled players, and there were so many secrets to be found that Easter egg hunters are still discovering bits, pieces, and oddities to this day.

If you haven't experienced "Super Mario 64" for yourself, give it a try.

I promise you won't be disappointed.

Here it is, the granddaddy of them all.

You knew it was going to end up on this list, as it routinely ends up on plenty of "greatest of all time" lists and sits comfortably atop the Metacritic rankings, but it's more than just numbers for "Ocarina of Time."

The game introduced a huge and expansive overworld map, a timeless story, and gameplay mechanics that set the bar for all 3D action-adventure games to come.

If you don't believe me, just look up "Z-Targeting."

The creators of "Ocarina of Time" literally invented a lock-on mechanic to help with 3D sword combat that every game since then has emulated in one way or another.

You want a memorable cast of characters? Check.

How about an iconic soundtrack? Check plus.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

No game will ever be able to replicate the sense of wonder "Ocarina of Time" created upon its release, and we as gamers have been chasing that high ever since.

Sure, games like "Breath of the Wild" have come close, but it will never feel the same as the first time we popped that golden cartridge into our N64's and stepped out into Hyrule Field for the first time.

Happy birthday, Nintendo 64! Thanks for the memories.

item.title: Macklin Celebrini is NHL's new highest-paid player after signing massive extension with Sharks
item.description: Macklin Celebrini's five-year, $18.8 million AAV extension makes him the NHL's highest-paid player, surpassing Leo Carlsson's recent Ducks deal.
item.content:encoded:
Anaheim Ducks forward Leo Carlsson's reign as the highest-paid player in the NHL didn't even last until the regular season, and that's because there's a new top dog on the paycheck front, and his name is Macklin Celebrini.

The San Jose Sharks' top pick in the 2024 NHL Draft signed a five-year extension that kicks in 2027-28 and is worth an AAV of $18.8 million per year.

That's $800,000 more than Carlsson will make this year.

If you had told me that 19- to 21-year-old NHLers would make more money in a season than LeBron James, I'd have insisted that you go seek professional help.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

But this is the reality we're living in, and players are getting paid.

"I couldn’t be happier to sign an extension today," Celebrini said, per NHL.com. "The faith and support that Mr. (Sharks owner Hasso) Plattner, Mike Grier and the entire staff have shown me throughout the past two seasons is proof that we are building something special here. My teammates and I are ready to take another step toward the ultimate goal of bringing a Stanley Cup to this city and its incredible fans. I can't wait to get going."

CONNOR BEDARD RE-SIGNS WITH BLACKHAWKS, ENDING HOPES FOR ANOTHER NHL OFFER SHEET THIS OFFSEASON

While it's a lot of coin, this was an incredibly smart move from Sharks GM Mike Grier.

Celebrini is the unquestioned centerpiece of a Sharks team with a lot of good young players like Will Smith and Michael Misa. Celebrini was set to be a restricted free agent next season, and there's no reason to think that he wouldn't re-sign in San Jose.

But Carlsson got his $18 million deal because the Ducks matched an offer sheet from the Philadelphia Flyers. The Sharks moved quickly, and by doing so, they prevented the possibility of an offer sheet. Plus, at the rate that NHL salaries and the salary cap are on the rise, it may only be a couple of years before $18.8 million looks like a team-friendly deal.

Especially if Celebrini follows up his massive sophomore season in which he put up 115 points (45 G, 70A) and earned himself a trip to the Olympics.

item.title: Super Bowl champion Plaxico Burress compares playing for Jets to his time in prison: 'A f—king loser'

item.title: Pope Leo promotes archbishop who barred Pelosi from Communion to one of Vatican's highest courts
item.description: Salvatore Cordileone, who barred Nancy Pelosi from Holy Communion over abortion rights, now joins the Vatican's highest court under Pope Leo XIV.
item.content:encoded:
Pope Leo XIV has appointed San Francisco Archbishop Salvatore Cordileone, who made international headlines after barring then-House Speaker Nancy Pelosi from receiving Holy Communion over her support for abortion rights, to serve on the Vatican's highest judicial body, in an announcement Saturday.

Cordileone was among seven clergy named to the Supreme Tribunal of the Apostolic Signatura, the Catholic Church's highest court after the pope. The appointment allows him to continue leading the Archdiocese of San Francisco while serving a five-year term on the Vatican tribunal, which oversees the administration of justice within the Church.

The Supreme Tribunal of the Apostolic Signatura is made up of cardinals, bishops and priests appointed by the pope for a term of five years, and is led by the Cardinal Prefect.

CATHOLIC CALIFORNIA UNIVERSITY TO HOST NANCY PELOSI AS COMMENCEMENT SPEAKER DESPITE ABORTION STANCE

In 2022, San Francisco Archbishop Salvatore Cordileone said that Pelosi would be banned from receiving Holy Communion in her own San Francisco Archdiocese because of her pro-abortion position.

"A Catholic legislator who supports procured abortion, after knowing the teaching of the Church, commits a manifestly grave sin which is a cause of most serious scandal to others," Cordileone wrote in a May 2022 letter. "Therefore, universal Church law provides that such persons ‘are not to be admitted to Holy Communion.'"

In a statement to Fox News Digital, Cordileone said he was honored by the appointment.

POPE LEO PLACES FORMER ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT IN CHARGE OF RED STATE DIOCESE

"I am deeply grateful to the Holy Father, Pope Leo XIV, for this appointment as a member of the Supreme Apostolic Signatura," Cordileone said. "I receive this responsibility with a profound sense of stewardship, recognizing that every office in the Church is entrusted for the service of Christ, His people, and the mission of the Gospel. The Supreme Apostolic Signatura assists the Holy Father in safeguarding the proper administration of justice within the life of the Church."

item.title: Josh Allen delivers full-throated unsolicited defense of Buffalo Bills' hideous new uniforms
item.description: The Bills quarterback urged fans to stop hating on the new gray alternate jerseys, calling them symbolic of newness as Buffalo moves forward.
item.content:encoded:
Josh Allen, arguably the NFL's best player, is a company man and great teammate for the Buffalo Bills, but Wednesday's defense of the indefensible new uniforms the team is rolling out in the coming NFL season was too much.

After the Bills finished their first practice, Allen sat down with reporters for his first news conference of training camp. The questions and answers were routine and mostly focused on all that is new with the club – new season, new coach, new schemes, new stadium.

JOSH ALLEN RECALLS HIS ROLE IN BILLS' COACHING SEARCH, DETAILS JOE BRADY’S APPROACH TO NEW ROLE

When the questions were seemingly all done, Allen pivoted to the team's new alternate uniforms.

Unsolicited, the quarterback took up defense for the so-called Nickel City unis. Those nickel gray uniforms include a "charge" helmet insignia but no trademark Buffalo. They are, the Bills say, inspired by grain elevators, steel mills and rail yards.

They are meant to represent the blue collar nature of the region.

Except a lot of folks both in the region and out hate them.

Hate.

"...Stop hating on the jerseys, guys," Allen said before he finished his news conference. "I don't know, if you guys are hating anything, I don't know. I don't see anything, but they're, they're great. I honestly like them.

"Speaking of new, right? It's a new look. It is. I understand that, but we gotta be new. And I think these jerseys kind of are symbolic of that. And I'm excited to wear them. We had a lot of people that put in a lot of hard work for these jerseys, and It just, it symbolizes a lot of newness, and that I am excited about."

Allen continued his defense of the gray duds when he was asked about last year's alternate all white uniform, which was well-received. Allen seemingly likes the grays better.

"We didn't win any games in all white, so absolutely," he said. "Otherwise, is that one or this one better than that? Time will tell.

"I've heard a lot of comments about the Jerseys. I enjoy them. I think it's very symbolic of what we want to do and what we want to be. I understand people want the old jerseys and the old helmets and all that, but at some point, too, we are moving forward. We have to move forward and do something new.

"That's what we're doing."

That is one way to think about this. But here's what the Bills should have done:

This year is the 250th anniversary of the United States. The NFL has embraced America 250 as a celebration. We've seen much love for the red, white and blue throughout the media, in the branding of national products, and obviously during the Independence Day holiday.

The Bills, coincidentally, boast red, white, and blue as their signature color scheme.

And nobody thought to make the obvious connection to America 250?

Nobody thought to somehow incorporate those national colors this year for the team's alternate uniform over "Nickel City" gray, which makes players more closely resemble Confederate soldiers?

The Bills have not yet announced when they will wear their alternate grays this season. They're expected to wear them twice.

item.title: Rand Paul seeks contempt charges after Fauci invokes Fifth Amendment more than 100 times
item.description: Rand Paul announced he will seek contempt charges after Anthony Fauci invoked his Fifth Amendment right over 100 times during the hearing.
item.content:encoded:
Dr. Anthony Fauci, the former National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) Director, left Wednesday's congressional grilling without answering lawmakers' questions, but Republicans are escalating their fight to compel his testimony.

Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., announced Wednesday that he will seek contempt charges against Fauci after he invoked his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination more than 100 times during the blockbuster hearing.

"We're going to have a vote next week on contempt. I think there's another legal question that the courts may have to decide upon," Paul said. "And that is whether or not a presidential pardon offers you complete immunity."

WATCH: FAUCI ATTORNEY EJECTED FROM SENATE HEARING AFTER CHAOTIC EXCHANGE: ‘YOU ARE NOT RECOGNIZED!’

The move capped off a years-long feud between Paul and Fauci after the senator accused Fauci of lying to Congress about the origins of COVID-19 and funding gain-of-function research in China that he alleged fueled the virus' outbreak.

Paul has previously issued criminal referrals against Fauci and suggested he should face criminal prosecution over alleged false statements to Congress.

Fauci has repeatedly denied Paul's allegations and said he did not do anything wrong.

Paul, the top Republican on the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, subpoenaed Fauci to testify Wednesday about the origins of COVID-19 after he declined to appear voluntarily.

Fauci repeatedly pleaded the Fifth, arguing Paul had an "obsession" with seeking his arrest and released more than 1,000 pages of his "personal diary" over the weekend in an effort to embarrass and intimidate him, according to his opening statement.

Fauci's refusal to answer any questions came as a surprise to Paul and his staff, who believed the ex-COVID-19 czar would not invoke his Fifth Amendment rights.

So confident, a source familiar told Fox News Digital, that several questions were prepared ahead of time, and members of the committee were told to come prepared for Fauci’s rebuttals.

Some Republicans on the panel have argued that the sweeping pardon former President Joe Biden granted Fauci would not shield him from contempt sanctions because any alleged misconduct would have occurred after the pardon was issued. 

The unprecedented pardon covers any federal offenses the ex-COVID-19 czar may have committed between Jan. 1, 2014, and Jan. 20, 2025 regarding his leadership over the NIAID and helming the nation’s COVID-19 response, among other government service.

"You don't have any rights under the Fifth Amendment because you've been pardoned," Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., said during the fiery hearing. "You know that. Your lawyer is sitting behind you now, shifting nervously in their chairs. They know it. This isn't about the Constitution. This isn’t about the law."

"This is about contempt, contempt for this body and contempt for the American people," he continued.

Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., said he was not surprised Fauci exercised his Fifth Amendment rights.

"I certainly understand why, on the advice of counsel, you're not answering any questions," Johnson said during the hearing. "Because I think it'd be almost impossible for you to answer the questions truthfully. Without really demonstrating what you did, your culpability."

After Fauci's lawyer, David Schertler, a prominent criminal defense attorney, attempted to speak without being recognized, Paul directed Capitol Police to eject him from the hearing room.

READ THE DIARIES: DOCUMENTS UNVEIL FAUCI'S THOUGHTS ON THE LAB-LEAK DEBATE, MASK DOUBTS AND TESTING FAILURES

The planned committee vote is likely to be along party lines as several Democrats on the panel came to Fauci’s defense on Wednesday.

If approved by the committee, the contempt resolution would head to the full Senate, where Democrats could filibuster it. The resolution would need 60 votes to advance, requiring at least some Democratic support. 

Democrats on the panel accused Paul of leading a partisan oversight investigation that cut them out, including failing to share documents before Republicans publicly released them. 

"This hearing appears to be a culmination of months of biased and selected efforts by the majority, under the guise of a committee investigation, to basically legitimize a predetermined conclusion that was reached years ago," Sen. Gary Peters, D-Mich., said during his opening statement.

The lead Democrat also accused Paul of "relitigating the past" instead of holding the annual threats hearing or an oversight hearing on the Department of Homeland Security's budget request for the upcoming fiscal year. 

Paul fired back that Peters’ claim that the committee blocked the minority from accessing records is "categorically false" and claimed the probe was the "most transparent investigation" in history.

"We actually created a website, and we put all of the information on the website. It continues to operate," Paul added. "The reason it hasn't been accessed is no Democrat ever signed up for it."

Sen. Maggie Hassan, D-N.H., also spoke at the hearing, arguing the forum was "designed to entrap" Fauci.

She and other Democrats were not able to ask any questions after Fauci repeatedly pleaded the Fifth.

item.title: Landon Donovan 'disappointed' Folarin Balogun red-card fiasco got 'out of hand' after Trump's involvement
item.description: Landon Donovan says the Folarin Balogun red card controversy "tainted" the USMNT's incredible World Cup run and motivated Belgium ahead of their match.
item.content:encoded:
Hindsight is 20/20, but it sure seems like Landon Donovan wishes the Folarin Balogun red-card controversy just played itself out.

The USMNT star received a red card in the round of 32 of the World Cup, which initially made him ineligible to play in the next round. However, FIFA decided to suspend the red card, which made Balogun eligible. President Donald Trump later said he called FIFA President Gianni Infantino and asked for a review, but FIFA claimed it was not influenced by Trump.

Nonetheless, the ruling added to what was already a huge controversy, and Donovan said the situation got "out of hand."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"I was disappointed... because it had been a World Cup full of nonpartisanship — people just loving America, loving the flag and loving what they were watching. Then it became very messy, and nobody wanted to see that, because we love the sport. We loved what we were watching, and the players have since admitted that it became difficult for them," Donovan told Fox News Digital in a recent interview. "It tainted what had been an incredible run.

"The really sad part is that it never should have been a red card, but that is the reality. It's just disappointing that it got out of control that way. I felt bad for Balogun. I felt bad for the team, to be honest, and it was very clear that it motivated the Belgian team."

The International Olympic Committee recently said it was not investigate Infantino regarding Trump's call to him.

IOC DECLINES TO INVESTIGATE GIANNI INFANTINO OVER TRUMP'S CALL ABOUT FOLARIN BALOGUN RED CARD

"All I did was I asked for a review because I didn’t think it was a foul," Trump said at the time. "And, again, I’m good at this stuff. I didn’t think it was a foul. I thought it was two great athletes who crashed into each other and got entangled. That was not a guy punching somebody in the face or anything, that would be different.

"I think it’s a terrible … if they wouldn’t allow a top player, maybe the best, maybe among the best on the team, to play. I think it would have had a big stain. I relayed it. I didn’t tell him what to do. I don’t believe he made the decision. I think it was a committee that made the decision, and they made the right decision because, No. 1, it wasn’t a foul, and you want to see a game with your best players."

As Donovan noted, Balogun admitted that the red card fiasco resulted in "a lot of outside noise" and caused "quite a bit of nerves" among the team.

"The closer we got to the game, I tried to just focus as best as I could, but it was difficult. A lot of outside noise and that’s hard to avoid," Balogun said earlier this month.

Belgium gave a strong response to Balogun being eligible for the game, but to no avail. At the end of the day, though, they got the last laugh with a 4-1 victory.

item.title: Why the under is the play as Trevor Rogers and Tarik Skubal face off in Baltimore-Detroit matchup
item.description: Tarik Skubal takes the mound in what could be his final Tigers start before the trade deadline as Baltimore's Trevor Rogers rides a hot streak.
item.content:encoded:
The trade deadline is looming, but that doesn't mean we are going to take our foot off the gas. I did mention it is smart to lower your unit size a bit on some of the baseball bets for the next couple of weeks, and I stand by that. You never know who will be part of a blockbuster trade, and you don't want your money tied up into something that isn't all that predictable. There isn't a bigger name available than the guy who is making a start today as the Orioles take on the Tigers.

The Baltimore Orioles season hasn't exactly gone to plan. They added Pete Alonso, and he has been a rewarding free agent, but the team is still hitting just .237 for the season. The pitching staff has a 4.21 ERA and a 1.35 WHIP. In the ultra-competitive American League East, there just isn't much room for error. They enter today's contest with a 52-56 record, which isn't terrible, but does probably put them in the seller conversation more than the buyer's room.

There is a lot of talent on the Orioles, but you have to wonder how they adjust for not only the remainder of this year, but next year too. They need help in the rotation, but their bullpen, a strength for so long, has actually been very good for the last couple of months. Maybe that's something to hang their hats on. Trevor Rogers takes the hill today with a 6-7 record, a 4.17 ERA, and a 1.27 WHIP. He's been fine, but nothing special. He has been better on the road than at home, with a 3.72 road ERA, and he has been great the past two months with just 11 earned runs allowed in 55 innings. Tigers hitters are batting .270 against him in 37 at-bats.

The Detroit Tigers are at a significant crossroads, and they also did not have this season go the way they intended. They will have plenty of people calling about a variety of their players. Their offense seems to have improved from last year, and their pitching looks about the same, but they haven't progressed from the slump they had to close last season. They are six games under .500 for the year and haven't played very well on the road this year.

As mentioned, no one will garner more attention than the man who takes the mound today for Detroit, Tarik Skubal. If you follow baseball at all, you know he is in the prime of his career, about to be a free agent, and has won the past two Cy Young awards. His numbers are still strong this year despite missing some time with injury. He is 7-5 with a 2.70 ERA and a 0.92 WHIP. He has been worse at home than on the road with a 3.46 home ERA. He has been his typical dominant self in July with a 1.48 ERA this month.

You do have to wonder if this is the last start that Skubal will make for the Tigers. If they don't trade him, they will let him walk for nothing as they are likely very far apart on a contract. Starters like this don't come around often, and the return has to make it worthwhile even if the Tigers still think they can make the postseason without him this year.

item.title: Oscar-winning singer Glen Hansard dead at 56
item.description: Glen Hansard, the Oscar-winning Irish singer-songwriter behind "Falling Slowly" and star of "Once," died at 56 in a motorcycle crash in Dublin.
item.content:encoded:
Irish singer-songwriter Glen Hansard, the Academy Award-winning musician behind the beloved song "Falling Slowly" and star of the acclaimed film "Once," has died after a motorcycle crash in Dublin. He was 56.

Hansard's management confirmed his death Wednesday, telling Irish broadcaster RTÉ that his family was "deeply shocked and heartbroken."

According to Irish police, a man in his 50s was killed in a single-vehicle motorcycle crash in Lucan, on the outskirts of Dublin, before 4:30 a.m. Wednesday. First responders treated the rider at the scene, but he was pronounced dead shortly after.

'IT TAKES TWO' RAPPER ROB BASE DEAD AT 59 AFTER CANCER FIGHT HE KEPT HIDDEN FROM FRIENDS

Hansard's legacy was tied to "Once," the 2007 Irish musical drama that transformed him from a respected hometown musician into an international star.

Starring opposite Markéta Irglová, Hansard played a struggling street musician whose connection with a fellow artist unfolds through music on the streets of Dublin.

The film became a global success, earning roughly $23 million at the worldwide box office and producing one of the decade's most memorable original songs, according to Rolling Stone.

GEORGE MICHAEL DIED WORTH $128M, BUT FRIENDS SAY HE SECRETLY GAVE AWAY MILLIONS FOR DECADES: AUTHOR

Hansard and Irglová won the Academy Award for best original song in 2008 for "Falling Slowly," a quiet acoustic ballad that became synonymous with the film.

Long before Hollywood recognition, Hansard had already established himself as one of Ireland's most respected performers.

Born in Ballymun, Dublin, in 1970, he began playing music as a teenager while busking throughout the city. 

In 1990, he founded The Frames, a band that developed a devoted following over several decades. Around the same time, Hansard expanded into acting, appearing as guitarist Outspan Foster in Alan Parker's 1991 film "The Commitments."

His career continued to evolve after "Once." Alongside Irglová, he formed The Swell Season while also maintaining an active solo career.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

His 2015 album "Didn't He Ramble" earned a Grammy nomination for Best Folk Album.

Hansard was equally recognized for the way he remained connected to Dublin's music community despite his international success.

Each Christmas Eve, he gathered fellow musicians outside Dublin's Gaiety Theatre for a charity busking tradition benefiting the Dublin Simon Community, an annual event that became a holiday fixture for locals.

He also played a prominent role during one of Ireland's most emotional public farewells.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

At the funeral of Pogues frontman Shane MacGowan in December 2023, Hansard and Irish singer Lisa O'Neill performed "Fairytale of New York," inspiring mourners throughout the church to sing and dance in celebration of MacGowan's life.

Hansard's reputation reached well beyond Ireland.

The Irish musician joined Bruce Springsteen onstage at Kilkenny's Nowlan Park in 2013 for a performance of "Drive All Night."

Tributes from across Ireland began pouring in within hours of news of his death.

Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin wrote on X that he was "deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Glen Hansard."

"A talented musician and actor who made a significant contribution to Ireland's cultural landscape over many years," Martin posted.

Waterboys frontman Mike Scott also reflected on Hansard's legacy, writing on X, "Just heard that Glen Hansard has died. Travel on well, Buddy. You made your dreams come true. I'm so sorry that he leaves his wife and 3-year-old child."

Hansard is survived by his partner, Finnish poet Maire Saaritsa, and their son, Christy, who was born in 2022.

His career leaves behind a catalog that stretched from Dublin sidewalks to the Oscar stage, making him one of Ireland's most enduring musical voices.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.
